items.summary: This archive contains supplementary code, data, finite certificates, and reproduction instructions for “Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces” by Makoto Ozawa (arXiv:2605.25322). This release accompanies the 41-page revision prepared in October 2026 and preserves all files from the two supplementary archives published in the previous Zenodo version. The computations concern embedded polygons in the simple cubic lattice under standard BFACF moves. Polygons are identified under translations, proper cubic rotations, cyclic changes of starting point, and reversal of traversal; spatial reflections are retained. The archive includes the original implementations, seed files, search summaries, and explicit merge-path certificates, together with the complete minimal-layer material for the figure-eight knot and the knot 6_3. For the figure-eight knot, four minimal-layer components at length 30 merge into one component at cap 32. For 6_3, twelve minimal-layer components at length 40 merge into two mirror-related branches at cap 42 and one branch at cap 44. These statements concern the branches originating in the minimal layers, rather than an enumeration of every component at higher caps. The new trefoil supplement certifies six nonminimal components born at length 26 for a fixed chirality. Five first meet the minimal layer at cap 28, whereas a 20-state component first meets it at cap 30. The archive supplies closed component lists, capped-component separation certificates, explicit connecting paths, verification programs, and audit logs. The individual component and exact merge-height certificates do not assume exhaustion of the length-26 population; exhaustiveness at that level remains conditional on the reported literature population. The trefoil material also includes the actual BFACF path used in Figure 2: 47 configurations connected by 46 moves, with maximum length 30. All coordinates, the complete sequence of configurations, figure-generation code, and independent transition checks are provided. Additional checks verify coordinate spans of the specified trefoil components and singleton capped components for supplied 48-edge representatives of 8_3 and 8_7, including an improper spatial symmetry of the 8_3 representative. The release includes the corresponding manuscript source and figures, current documentation, checksums, provenance records, and a verification runner. Historical manuscripts are retained separately in the legacy directory; the current manuscript source is arxiv_revision/main.tex. The documentation distinguishes certified finite results from conditional completeness statements and open questions concerning eventual connectivity, Gordian configurations, and unbounded strong local-minimum birth levels. Requirements: Python 3 for the verification scripts and a C++17 compiler for the large capped-component audits. Regenerating the trefoil figures additionally requires NumPy and Matplotlib. Detailed commands and the scope of each verification are given in the included README files.

items.summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.
items.title: Structural Decipherment Without Lexical Recovery: A Cross-Validated Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript

items.summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-three entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.
items.title: jerlov: inherent optical properties of the Jerlov optical water types, with provenance

items.summary: A harness wraps one or more generators (language models, other neural models, programs or people) with a symbolic layer: a rule set and, optionally, a knowledge store. A checker evaluates each candidate output against the rules and returns a verdict and the violated rules. A release gate lets the output, or part of it, leave only when it passes or under an exception policy, fixed in advance or chosen per request. That is the minimal core. Optional modules, used alone or in any combination, extend it. Rules may filter inputs, decoding, finished outputs, agent actions before execution, and outputs already delivered. A failing output may be repaired by a minimal symbolic change, or revised under a budget the generator cannot alter, with the passing part released under caveats. A passing output may carry a receipt tied to the state it was checked against, so that a later change re-checks affected outputs and supersedes a receipt only when its verdict changes (or, optionally, when the facts it records change). The rule set may improve from evidence, each change held inactive until it passes a gate that can refuse unapproved weakening and require independent approval. Further modules separate claims from outcomes, count correlated sources once, re-extract rendered prose, replay decisions, accept statements by cost, add human review, and turn the harness's verdicts, repairs and revisions into training signals. Outputs may also be read into typed records before checking, with size caps and a per-rule estimate of evaluation work, or a step counter, so that each check made by a rule whose work can be estimated or counted is bounded in advance, and a request may bring rules of its own, written by the generator or another source and admitted only when they cannot relax the rules in force. Knowledge and policy changes can then be made in rules instead of model weights, and any fine-tuning that remains needs less manual labelling.
items.title: Rule-Gated Generation: A Harness That Filters, Repairs, Certifies and Re-Checks Machine-Generated Output and Improves Its Own Rules Under a Gate

items.summary: Benchmark data and trained interatomic potentials accompanying Learning nonlocal residuals in interatomic potentials with Fourier neural operators , by Wei Chen and Gian-Marco Rignanese. The files are organized into five benchmarks: homogeneous Yukawa interactions, heterogeneous screening, liquid water, LLZO, and Au2/MgO(001). Each benchmark archive contains its datasets and exact splits, final checkpoints and required local backbones, training recipes, generation or preparation scripts, and evaluation provenance. A shared archive supplies inference code, loading instructions, model indices, and checksums. The collection contains 422 result entries referencing 376 distinct checkpoints: 274 primary entries, 115 appendix entries, ten molecular-dynamics model entries, and 23 diagnostic entries. The heterogeneous benchmark includes the 40-set remote-medium probe. The homogeneous benchmark includes thirty production molecular-dynamics trajectories totaling 12 ns and 24,030 saved frames. Training recipes use YAML for MACE, LES, and FNO, JSON for CACE and CACE-SOG, and the published shell command for the upstream Au2/MgO MACE1 model. Download the shared archive and the desired benchmark archives, then extract them in the same directory. See README.md and the per-benchmark license notices.

items.summary: LONGITUDINAL DEVICE MIGRATION AND MEANING CONTINUITY AT THE LIMIT Device Replacement × Model Bridging × Control Semantics STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 24 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Research Works This research monograph investigates a deceptively difficult question in long-term brain–computer interfaces: when sensors, acquisition electronics, firmware, electrode geometry, or decoding models change, what would justify the claim that a user's task-grounded control meaning has been preserved? Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?

This release accompanies the 41-page revision prepared in October 2026 and preserves all files from the two supplementary archives published in the previous Zenodo version. The computations concern embedded polygons in the simple cubic lattice under standard BFACF moves. Polygons are identified under translations, proper cubic rotations, cyclic changes of starting point, and reversal of traversal; spatial reflections are retained. The archive includes the original implementations, seed files, search summaries, and explicit merge-path certificates, together with the complete minimal-layer material for the figure-eight knot and the knot 6_3. For the figure-eight knot, four minimal-layer components at length 30 merge into one component at cap 32. For 6_3, twelve minimal-layer components at length 40 merge into two mirror-related branches at cap 42 and one branch at cap 44. These statements concern the branches originating in the minimal layers, rather than an enumeration of every component at higher caps. The new trefoil supplement certifies six nonminimal components born at length 26 for a fixed chirality. Five first meet the minimal layer at cap 28, whereas a 20-state component first meets it at cap 30. The archive supplies closed component lists, capped-component separation certificates, explicit connecting paths, verification programs, and audit logs. The individual component and exact merge-height certificates do not assume exhaustion of the length-26 population; exhaustiveness at that level remains conditional on the reported literature population. The trefoil material also includes the actual BFACF path used in Figure 2: 47 configurations connected by 46 moves, with maximum length 30. items.summary: Four-dimensional beam-matrix reconstruction from quadrupole scans is the standard way to mea- sure cross-plane coupling and the intrinsic emittances that a decoupling section can recover. We show that a scan of a single thin quadrupole, normal or skew and placed anywhere in a linear lattice, determines at most nine of the ten beam-matrix parameters for any number of settings, because each measured second moment is quadratic in the quadrupole strength. The unmeasured direction lies in the x–y cross block and has a closed form in terms of the transfer matrices; for a quadrupole followed by a drift of length L its nonzero entries are Wxpy = Wpxy = 1 and Wpxpy = −2/L. Both projected emittances are therefore measured, but the beam matrices consistent with the data form a line segment along which the smaller intrinsic emittance ranges from zero to slightly above its true value, so a single-knob scan gives only an upper bound on it. A thick quadrupole restores the miss- ing direction only weakly, its singular value scaling approximately as the sixth power of the magnet length. Scanning two independently powered quadrupoles of any type makes the reconstruction well posed without additional hardware.

items.summary: This archive is provided as artifact material for the article "Synthesis and Verification of Register Automata over Data Sequences" for SETTA 2026. Abstract: Data sequences, such as time series, traces, and sensor streams, are words over large or infinite data domains. Their properties often depend on comparisons between values at different positions, which finite automata cannot express directly. We study synthesis and verification for Deterministic Register Automata (DRAs) over ordered data sequences. DRAs combine finite control with registers for remembered data values, providing compact symbolic descriptions of quantitative sequence languages. Our technical core is a local-search synthesis procedure and an exact robustness checker for DRAs. We fix the alphabet theory to ordered rationals $(\Q;<,=)$ with rational guard constants and use non-negative affine accumulator costs. For a fixed number of DRA registers, the checker runs in polynomial time; its dependence on that number is exponential. It reduces robustness to coverability and then to a shortest-path problem. Since the search ranges over $\Q^+$, it produces variable-length witnesses and, for RAA-definable alignment costs such as DTW, explores a counterexample space with no a priori length bound. As an application, we use learned DRAs as interpretable surrogates for queried neural sequence classifiers. A probably approximately correct (PAC) validation loop refines rejected candidates, returns genuine non-robustness witnesses for the classifier when found, and accepts a surrogate only with statistical guarantees for fidelity and local stability. We implement the framework in \textit{RAExc}, enabling the synthesis of interpretable automata and the verification of their robustness. We evaluate the approach on benchmark languages and sequentialized MNIST, demonstrating high accuracy while verifying the robustness of the learned automata.

items.summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. items.summary: This dataset provides computational supplements, source code, finite-state component data, and independently checkable BFACF certificates for Makoto Ozawa, "Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces" (arXiv:2605.25322). The data concern self-avoiding polygons in the simple cubic lattice under standard BFACF moves and a lattice-length filtration. The earlier release documents the complete minimal-layer merge trees of $4_1$ (four components at length 30 merging at length 32) and $6_3$ (twelve components at length 40, two at length 42, and one at length 44). It also documents selected nonminimal trefoil components born at length 26; these selected births are not claimed to exhaust the full filtered graph. The frozen-unknot construction consists of a 64-edge Hamiltonian lattice unknot with no length-preserving or length-decreasing BFACF moves. An independently verified sequence of 25,436 BFACF moves reduces it to the elementary square with peak length 66. A two-edge block-splicing construction gives frozen unknots of length $64m$ for every integer $m\ge1$. New in the 19 October 2026 update: A minimal 24-edge trefoil is spliced to the 64-edge frozen unknot to produce an explicit 88-edge trefoil admitting no length-nonincreasing BFACF moves. The additional files supply the lattice direction words and coordinates, connected-sum construction, local-move verifier, and sampled checks for $m=1,2,3,4,8,16$. Repeating the frozen unknot block before the final trefoil splice gives frozen trefoils of length $64m+24$ for every $m\ge1$; reflection gives both chiralities. The results imply infinitely many nonminimal strong local-minimum births for the unknot and for both trefoil chiralities, within the standard BFACF filtration. The exact merge height 66 is established only for the 64-edge unknot. For longer frozen unknots and trefoils the proofs give lower bounds $H(P_m,U)\ge64m+2$ and $H(R_m,Q)\ge64m+26$, respectively; no exact merge heights or unbounded minimax excess are claimed. The construction is discrete and does not establish a positive barrier in continuous ropelength-filtered knot spaces or a universal result for arbitrary knot types. The archive retains earlier datasets and provenance information. Reproducibility instructions identify which outputs come from complete finite enumeration, certified BFACF paths, protected-port constructions, or limited computational checks.

items.summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.

items.summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. items.summary: This archive is provided as artifact material for the article "Synthesis and Verification of Register Automata over Data Sequences" for SETTA 2026. Abstract: Data sequences, such as time series, traces, and sensor streams, are words over large or infinite data domains. Their properties often depend on comparisons between values at different positions, which finite automata cannot express directly. We study synthesis and verification for Deterministic Register Automata (DRAs) over ordered data sequences. DRAs combine finite control with registers for remembered data values, providing compact symbolic descriptions of quantitative sequence languages. Our technical core is a local-search synthesis procedure and an exact robustness checker for DRAs. We fix the alphabet theory to ordered rationals $(\Q;<,=)$ with rational guard constants and use non-negative affine accumulator costs. For a fixed number of DRA registers, the checker runs in polynomial time; its dependence on that number is exponential. It reduces robustness to coverability and then to a shortest-path problem. Since the search ranges over $\Q^+$, it produces variable-length witnesses and, for RAA-definable alignment costs such as DTW, explores a counterexample space with no a priori length bound. As an application, we use learned DRAs as interpretable surrogates for queried neural sequence classifiers. A probably approximately correct (PAC) validation loop refines rejected candidates, returns genuine non-robustness witnesses for the classifier when found, and accepts a surrogate only with statistical guarantees for fidelity and local stability. We implement the framework in \textit{RAExc}, enabling the synthesis of interpretable automata and the verification of their robustness. We evaluate the approach on benchmark languages and sequentialized MNIST, demonstrating high accuracy while verifying the robustness of the learned automata.
